identityReview: Marine Le Pen, born August 5, 1968 in Neuilly-sur-Seine; not Jean-Marie Le Pen or Marion Maréchal. Paris II maîtrise 1990, criminal-law DEA 1991 and CAPA 1992, no doctorate. Lawyer before party legal work. Former FN/RN president, succeeded permanently by Bardella November 5, 2022 after interim period. Current Pas-de-Calais constituency 11 deputy; former RN parliamentary group president following Chenu replacement recorded October 27 and published October 28, 2026. Three prior presidential campaigns, two runoffs, no presidential victory. Appeal conviction persists under further legal review, not a final acquittal or established future presidency.
lifeStatusEvidence: Euronews November 16, 2026 reports a completed meeting with Ukrainian ambassador to France Vadym Omelchenko, including statements attributed to the RN communiqué. The account distinguishes that meeting from a proposed future meeting with Zelensky. No original video/audio watched; a November 16 television-debate preview is not used as proof of attendance.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read Assembly current and historical records, Institut Montaigne biographies, Le Parisien/RTL leadership reports, Interior Ministry final presidential tables, Public Sénat legislative and legal reporting, Reuters appeal report, Actu-Juridique legal analysis, Légifrance official group-change notice and Euronews completed-meeting report. Read Commons candidate/parent metadata and original Flickr CC0 link. No portrait pixels.
corrections: Read current Assembly profile: born August 5, 1968 in Neuilly-sur-Seine, lawyer, current RN deputy for Pas-de-Calais constituency 11. Current membership does not imply continued group presidency; the October replacement notice supersedes stale summaries. No contact details or personal correspondence used.

Read Sycomore mandates: June 21, 2017–June 21, 2022; June 22, 2022–June 9, 2024; current term from July 1, 2024. Formal mandate starts are distinct from election days. Do not claim an uninterrupted mandate through dissolution or confuse presidential and legislative elections.

Read Institut Montaigne’s 2015 biography: Paris II maîtrise 1990, criminal-law DEA 1991, CAPA 1992; first regional mandate 1998, January 2011 party congress, third place in 2012. Diploma nomenclature preserved rather than converting DEA into a PhD. Its municipal chronology is not relied on; omit unsupported exact dates from conflicting summaries.

Read Institut Montaigne’s 2022 candidate biography: Paris legal practice, 1998 move to party legal service, 2004/2009/2014 European elections, national deputy from 2017 and 2018 party renaming. Its July 2021 stepping-back shorthand is distinguished from Bardella’s September interim start and November 2022 permanent election. Stale candidate/current-role labels are not carried into 2026.

Read contemporary Le Parisien January 16, 2011 report, not merely the title. Official result at Tours: succession to Jean-Marie Le Pen after defeating Bruno Gollnisch. Earlier leaks and later publication in another newspaper are not the formal succession date. No need to reproduce family details or assign her father’s legal record to her.

Read RTL November 5, 2022 report: Bardella elected permanent president, interim presidency since September 13, 2021; party formerly FN, renamed RN in 2018. Interim party management, permanent party presidency and Assembly group leadership are three distinct roles.

Read Interior Ministry’s final national 2017 election table: May 7 runoff, Le Pen 10638475 votes and 33.90% of valid votes, Macron winner. The table separately lists registered-elector percentages and first-round figures; those denominators and rounds are not mixed.

Read Interior Ministry’s final national 2022 table: April 24 runoff, Le Pen 13288686 votes and 41.45% of valid votes, Macron winner. Do not substitute early estimates, percentage of registered voters, first-round share or legislative seat totals.

Read Public Sénat’s July 1, 2024 roundup of the June 30 first round. Le Pen won constituency 11 with 32681 votes and 58.04%. Publication after midnight is not the election date; official Sycomore establishes July 1 mandate start. No full constituency ballot recount performed.

Read Reuters’s July 7, 2026 completed-judgment and interview report via Investing.com. Conviction upheld, reduced electoral penalty, candidacy announcement and denial are separate facts. Later legal debate qualifies the initial report’s apparent certainty about eligibility; announcing cassation is not a final acquittal.

Read Actu-Juridique’s substantive legal analysis: March 31, 2025 and July 7, 2026 sentences, no provisional execution in the appeal ruling, cassation filings, constitutional questions and disputed suspensive effects. December 16 QPC hearing and early-April 2027 target are reported future plans, not completed rulings. Analysis is not the underlying judgment or an authoritative final eligibility determination.

Read Public Sénat November 2, 2026 explanation of divergent positions. Rémy Heitz rejects revival of the first judgment; Didier Guérin argues original provisional ineligibility persists. Other cited lawyers also disagree. Public copy preserves the dispute without declaring a new court decision, certain disqualification or conclusively certified eligibility. The five-year initial ban is not represented as the unchanged latest sentence.

Read Légifrance’s original October 28, 2026 JORF notice, NOR INPA2628758X: Assembly president informed that Sébastien Chenu replaces Le Pen as RN group president. Publication is distinguished from the Assembly’s October 27 record and October 24 political announcement. No claim of resignation from her parliamentary seat.

Read Euronews’s November 16, 2026 completed ambassador-meeting account, attributed partly to an RN communiqué. Meeting with Vadym Omelchenko is retrospective; possible future Zelensky meeting is not completed. Campaign aid-policy proposals are not enacted government decisions. July 2026 illustration caption is not the meeting date, and the source’s financial totals were not independently audited.

Read Assembly 2026 group-change page: replacement of Le Pen by Chenu under October 27 heading, JORF October 28. November 16/17 dates at the top concern a different member’s group change and must not be attached to the RN presidency. Confirms current deputy/former group-president correction.

additionalConsulted.access: Read biography confirming 1992–1998 Paris legal practice, 1998 legal-service transition, early mandates and 2011 succession. Historical interpretive claims about other politicians’ motives are not adopted.

Search excerpt places legal qualifications a year later. Full PDF not reviewed; public copy follows the more specific readable Montaigne chronology, corroborated by Europe 1 indexing, not the conflicting dates.

Followed Actu-Juridique’s link; only one unreadable line returned. Court communiqué itself not reviewed. Future procedure described only as reported legal-analysis context, not a completed judgment.
Read October 24 announcement, distinguishing it from formal Assembly October 27 record and October 28 publication.
Read original source caption, February 8 taken/upload date and clicked Public domain link to actual CC0 1.0 deed. Do not confuse this dedication with the different Public Domain Mark.
Read parent history, dimensions, licence verification and EXIF photographer credit. Camera metadata is not visual inspection.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No full trial/appeal case file, original cassation communiqué body, final future eligibility decision, degree certificates, constituency ballot recount, original meeting video/audio or portrait pixels reviewed. Press legal interpretations are explicitly distinguished from judgments; political campaign statements are not implemented government policy.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields reviewed in seven foreign languages against Chinese and English. Preserve current deputy/former party and group president; maîtrise/DEA/CAPA chronology and no doctorate; 2011 succession, 2021 interim versus November 2022 permanent successor; 2017/2022 final runoff numbers and valid-vote denominators; June 30, 2024 election versus July 1 mandate; March 31, 2025 initial sentence versus July 7, 2026 reduced sentence; suspended prison years and suspended ineligibility months; disputed cassation effects rather than final eligibility; October 27 record versus October 28 publication; November 16 completed meeting. German corrected to change in group leadership rather than change of party group.
